title: A dual-region ytterbium tweezer apparatus with an in-vacuum nanofiber cavity
authors: Shunichiro Hashimoto, Hideki Ozawa, Yusuke Hisai, Takao Aoki, Ryotaro Inoue
abstract: We present a dual-region experimental apparatus for trapping single atoms of the fermionic isotope ytterbium-171 (${}^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$) with optical tweezers in a science chamber containing an in-vacuum nanofiber cavity. A source region is located approximately $240\,\mathrm{mm}$ from the science chamber, preserving optical access around the chamber for high-numerical-aperture tweezer optics. A pulsed transport sequence based on longitudinal moving molasses launches atomic pulses toward the science chamber, where they are decelerated and recaptured in a magneto-optical trap. We subsequently load single atoms into a $2\times2$ tweezer array located approximately $50\,\mathrm{μm}$ from the nanofiber and measure a $1/e$ lifetime of $9.5(7)\,\mathrm{s}$. These results demonstrate that the dual-region architecture provides sufficient ${}^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ atoms for single-atom tweezer operation near an in-vacuum nanofiber cavity.
summary: The authors report the successful construction and operation of a dual-region apparatus designed to trap single fermionic ytterbium atoms near an in-vacuum nanofiber cavity. They overcome challenges in atom delivery by implementing a pulsed transport sequence, enabling single-atom loading into an optical tweezer array. The key achievement is demonstrating stable, multi-second trapping of single atoms in this complex, integrated quantum system.
main_problem: The primary goal was to develop and demonstrate a dual-region apparatus capable of trapping single fermionic ytterbium atoms near an in-vacuum nanofiber cavity.
main_result: The system successfully demonstrated single-atom loading into a tweezer array near the cavity and achieved a measurable single-atom trapping lifetime of 9.5(7) seconds.
method: The experiment utilized a pulsed transport sequence based on longitudinal moving molasses to move atoms from a source region to a science chamber containing the trapping optics.
model_or_system: The platform involves a dual-region setup using fermionic ytterbium-171 atoms. Atoms are cooled and transported using $399	ext{ nm}$ light, captured in a $3	ext{D-MOT}$ ($556	ext{ nm}$), and finally loaded into optical tweezers positioned near an in-vacuum nanofiber cavity.
key_observables: Single-atom filling fraction (up to 74.9%), $1/e$ trap lifetime (9.5(7) s), and the number of atoms delivered during transport.
important_parameters: Source-to-science chamber distance ($\approx 240	ext{ mm}$), tweezer array distance from nanofiber ($\approx 50\ \mu	ext{m}$), and optimal transport parameters (e.g., $t_{	ext{launch}} \simeq 1.2 	ext{ ms}$).
main_assumptions: The design assumes that the dual-region architecture can provide sufficient atom flux while maintaining optical access and protecting the nanofiber cavity from untrapped atoms.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview of the dual-region apparatus and single-atom tweezer operation, while Figure 2 characterizes the pulsed transport sequence by showing atom number versus time of flight and launch duration.
paper_structure: The paper details the development of the dual-region apparatus, characterizes the pulsed atom transport sequence from the source to the science chamber, demonstrates single-atom loading into the tweezer array near the cavity, and finally reports the measured trapping lifetime.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines state-of-the-art techniques in cold atom trapping (moving molasses, MOTs) with advanced quantum optics elements (in-vacuum nanofiber cavities) for fundamental quantum physics experiments.
